source.title_on_document: Generative artificial intelligence, human creativity, and art

supplement.where: PNAS Nexus online, file pgae052_Supplementary_Data.pdf (24 pages); read via Europe PMC supplementaryFiles for PMC10914360
supplement.holds: Sample counts and user-month summary statistics (Table S1), heterogeneity regression (Table S3), aggregate ATTs under measurement-error simulations (Tables S4 and S5), event-study ATTs with standard errors and 95 percent bounds for productivity, value, and mean/min/max Content and Visual Novelty (Tables S6 to S9), and generalized synthetic control results (Tables S10 to S13). The main text reports the novelty effects only as figures.

paper_design_summary: The authors use the full posting histories (January 2022 to June 2023) of over 53,000 users of a large art-sharing platform, of whom over 5,800 adopted text-to-image AI, identified from AI tags on their posts. An event-study difference-in-differences (Callaway and Sant'Anna, doubly robust) compares adopters with never-treated and not-yet-treated users on monthly posts, favorites per view, and Content and Visual Novelty, defined as the cosine distance of each artwork's BLIP-2/SBERT caption embedding or DINOv2 image embedding from all earlier artworks. No one was assigned to AI.

studies.label: Art-sharing platform panel, AI adopters vs non-adopters (event-study DiD)

participants.exclusions: Panel winsorized to drop users with extreme pretreatment activity; Table S1 lists 4,764 adopters and 40,275 non-adopters after winsorizing (SI p. 2). Novelty was computed for all adopters' artworks and a random sample of 10,000 control users (SI p. 3, Section 1C).
participants.who: Users who declared they produce 'Digital Art' on one of the largest art-sharing platforms (platform not named); over 53,000 users, over 4.3 million artworks, over 5,800 known AI adopters. Analysis panel at the user-month level.
participants.quote: We received a panel of the entire publishing histories of over 53,000 unique users on the platform from January of 2022 until June of 2023, consisting of over 4.3 million digital artworks
participants.locator: SI p. 2, Section 1A and Table S1; main text Introduction

ai_tool.name_model: Text-to-image generative AI (Midjourney, Stable Diffusion, DALL-E, etc.), adoption identified by keyword matching on post titles and tags and by posts in AI art communities
ai_tool.how_used: Artists chose to use text-to-image tools in their own work; adoption date is the user's first known AI-generated post.

task.description: Digital artworks posted to an art-sharing platform
task.duration: Panel from January 2022 to June 2023; event windows from 3 months before to 7 months after adoption

outcomes.name: Mean Content Novelty (cosine distance of BLIP-2 caption SBERT embedding to all prior artworks, mean per artwork, user-month)
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Content Novelty uses pairwise cosine distances between BLIP-2 caption embeddings from Sentence-BERT and earlier artworks; the panel is aggregated monthly (main article, Materials and methods, Measuring creative novelty and Content feature extraction; SI pp. 2-3, Sections 1A and 1C-1D). Minimum Content Novelty is retained here as a measurement variant: aggregate ATT (original) -0.0154 (SI p. 10, Table S4); event-study month 0 ATT -0.0101* (SE 0.0034; 95% confidence bounds [-0.0197, -0.0005]); Observations 43,126 (SI p. 18, Table S8). The observation count is user-months, not distinct people. Standard errors are clustered at the user level; * marks significance at the 95% confidence level. Generalized synthetic control robustness results appear in SI p. 21, Table S11 (mean), and p. 22, Table S12 (minimum).

outcomes.name: Creative productivity: log monthly artwork posts (user-month)
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Log of the number of artifacts a user posts in a month (main article, Results, Creative productivity, Fig. 1a). The analysis uses a monthly panel: n_units counts user-month observations, not distinct people (SI p. 2, Section 1A; p. 16, Table S6). Event-study ATT estimates use a doubly robust estimator with standard errors clustered at the user level; * marks significance at the 95% confidence level (SI p. 16, Table S6). Generalized synthetic control robustness results are reported in SI p. 20, Table S10.

eligibility.reason: Observational platform data: users self-selected into text-to-image AI, and adoption was inferred from post tags; effects come from an event-study difference-in-differences against never-treated and not-yet-treated users. No one was randomly assigned to AI. Novelty is each artwork's embedding distance from all earlier platform artworks, scored on real output.

one_line_finding: After adopting text-to-image AI, artists' mean Content Novelty fell (aggregate ATT -0.0088) and mean Visual Novelty fell (-0.0409), maximum Content Novelty rose slightly (0.0032), and favorites per view rose from about 2 percent to 3 percent by month six (SI p. 10, Table S4; main text, Fig. 1).
